messages:
Lena K: quick heads-up — onboarding qwen-slim-v1 with int8 dynamic showed a ~3-5% drop on our codegen eval compared to fp16. not huge but reproducible across seeds.

Omar: thanks lena. any sign it's from model weights vs tokenization?

Lena K: initial bisect points to the quant path. but also noticed weird token id collisions when using the legacy bpe merges we ship for compat. some ids map to the same embedding index in our convert script.

Ben M: do you have an example mapping? that could explain kv-cache misalignment if ids are remapped after cache build.

Lena K: sure — minimal repro:

```
# pseudo dump from converter
old_id: 423 -> new_id: 423
old_id: 1024 -> new_id: 423  # collision
```

Lena K: when that happens the prefix keys are stored using the old ids then looked up with the new ids at decode time.

Omar: that explains a lot. i also ran a headwise compare and saw per-head attention magnitudes diverge after ~8 tokens when quantized. could be rotary phase handling differs between our kernel and the upstream qwen reference.

Ben M: are we applying a per-head scale for rotary? i remember earlier qwen variants used a headwise phase scaling trick. if the runtime applies scaling before quant or after, quant error can leak into logits.

Priya: fwiw i reproduced the token alias locally — converter script uses a dict that loses order and collapses merges with identical posterior ids. simple fix is to keep first-seen mapping and assert no duplicates. pushing a patch in a sec.

Lena K: nice. i'll re-run the int8 workflow once that's in.

ci-bot: build 2026.03.20.451 passed (converter-fix) :white_check_mark:

Ben M: re: rotary — here's a tiny diff i ran to flip when scale applied:

```py
# before: scale after rotary
rotary_out = apply_rotary(x, sincos)
rotary_out = rotary_out * head_scale
# after: scale before rotary
x_scaled = x * head_scale
rotary_out = apply_rotary(x_scaled, sincos)
```

Ben M: doing the scale-before makes quant noise propagate differently. on qwen-slim-v1 fp16 vs int8 gap shrunk by ~1.8% in our microbench.

Omar: good find. can you add a tiny test that checks kv cache identity across a short prefix with both implementations? that should catch remapping/misalignment.

Priya: patch landed: 1894500123-converter-preserve-firstmap. also added an extra assert to fail onboarding if any new_id duplicates appear.

Lena K: re-run results: after converter fix + headwise scale-before change the codebench delta is down to ~0.9%. still investigating residuals (probably quant noise on long-range attention).

Ben M: for the residuals i suggest running long-context logits comparisons with randomly rotated phase seeds — if mismatch correlates with token positions we can pin to rotary-phase drift.

Omar: i'll spin up 4 runs with context lengths [64, 256, 1024, 2048] and both fp16/int8 for the same seed. should be done later today.

Lena K: thanks all. next steps: (1) keep converter assert in CI (2) land headwise scale-before as an opt-in flag for now (3) Omar to post long-context diffs.

Priya: also added a short note in onboarding checklist: "verify tokenizer id uniqueness + kv-cache replay test".

ci-bot: test matrix queued on infra-ml-host (4 jobs).

Omar: queued jobs finished. initial matrix shows mismatch increases with context length but plateaus after ~1024 — attaching logs to the PR.

Lena K: excellent. will open follow-up for exploring quant-aware calibration on rotary params (small KL-targeted calibration set).

Ben M: :thumbsup:

Priya: great teamwork — keeping this model in the pipeline.

ci-bot: thread closed due to inactivity after 2 days."
